target_customer: Hospitals and clinicians who order routine lab tests
problem: Routine lab results contain information that could flag acute conditions early, but clinicians lack tools to read it. Biocogniv builds AI that analyzes standard lab test results to support diagnosis and predict outcomes.
business_model: B2B software licensed to hospitals and health systems

founders.name: Artur Adib
founders.background_notes: Founding team member and head of software at BETA Technologies; Twitter engineer before IPO; principal engineer at Magic Leap.

technical_complexity.rationale: Clinical AI needs hospital data access, model validation and FDA pathway work; a small team faces regulatory and data hurdles.

defensibility.rationale: FDA clearance and validated clinical data are hard to replicate, but EHR vendors could build similar predictors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Epic built its own sepsis model; directories report Biocogniv was later acquired, with the buyer unconfirmed.

market_need_then: Hospitals were under strain in 2020 with COVID-19, and interest in AI to triage patients from lab tests rose; the company's early work included COVID-related marks and tools.

branding.domain_note: Used biocogniv.com, which no longer resolved from the research environment.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press or community around the brand was found beyond trademark records; name is a technical blend of bio and cognition.

outcome_analysis: Biocogniv, founded by an engineer with physics and software leadership experience, raised a reported $6M seed in August 2020 and pursued AI diagnostics from routine lab tests. Directories mark it as acquired and one reports BETA Technologies as buyer, but no deal terms, date or announcement were found, so the outcome quality and reasons are not public.
notes: biocogniv.com failed DNS resolution, treated as dead. Acquirer BETA Technologies and year 2026 come from one directory profile only, unverified, so not recorded as acquirer. Aggregator funding totals conflict ($5.0M to $17.08M) and a $5.0M October 2023 round is unverified. The $6M seed is reported by aggregators and one VC portfolio page, not a primary news article. Dascena listed without dated source. The YC page gave no product description; product details come from directories. Dascena was a sepsis AI competitor but no source dated to 2020 was found, so the list is empty.
